commit 8af59b2e7a91c227081617240e98aa282eadc5f9
Author: Olatunji Ruwase <tunji.ruwase@snowflake.com>
Date:   Fri Nov 6 11:21:30 2026 +0000

    Restore fp32 masters for ZeRO-3 and the ZeRO-1 BF16 optimizer (#8892)
    
    ## Summary
    - Follow-up to #8891 (merged as `2dd22dc`). The delta against `master`
    is ZeRO-3 and the dedicated ZeRO-1 BF16 optimizer, plus the review fixes
    listed below.
    - `load_checkpoint` still always restores saved fp32 masters.
    `load_optimizer_states=False` keeps those masters and starts Adam with
    fresh moments. `load_module_only=True` rebuilds the dedicated BF16
    optimizer from the loaded bf16 weights. ZeRO-3 still reads its fp32
    partition on a module-only load, because the model checkpoint does not
    hold the partitioned weights.
    - `ZeRO-3` and `BF16_Optimizer.load_state_dict(...,
    load_from_fp32_weights=False)` now rebuild the masters from the bit16
    weights, matching ZeRO stage 1 and 2. `DeepSpeedEngine.load_checkpoint`
    passes true, so a normal resume keeps the saved masters.
    `zero_optimization.load_from_fp32_weights` stays deprecated and ignored.
    - Review fixes: a pipeline-serialized load now checks that ZeRO shards
    exist before waiting on the previous rank, so a missing shard raises
    instead of leaving ranks blocked in `dist.recv`. A universal load that
    skips optimizer state keeps `optim_fragment`, so
    `safe_get_full_optimizer_state` and `safe_set_full_optimizer_state`
    still work. A leftover debug `print` in `BF16_Optimizer` is removed.
    
    AI assistance was used to implement and test this change. This does not
    duplicate an open DeepSpeed PR.
    
    ## Test plan
    - [x] CPU, torch 2.9.1+cu130, Python 3.12.12, Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C,
    gloo, world size 1, `tests/unit/checkpoint/test_fp32_master_only.py` and
    `tests/unit/checkpoint/test_fp32_master_stage3_bf16.py`: 10 passed. Both
    files ran on the tree that became `a22f0cc4`.
    - The dedicated BF16 optimizer keeps the saved masters when optimizer
    state is skipped and rebuilds them for `load_module_only=True`. ZeRO-3
    keeps the saved masters for both of those loads. Adam moments stay
    fresh.
    - A direct `load_state_dict(..., load_from_fp32_weights=False)` after a
    module-only load rebuilds the masters from the bit16 weights, for both
    BF16 and ZeRO-3.
    - Optimizer globals (`clip_grad`, `overflow`, `dynamic_loss_scale`) are
    not restored on a masters-only load.
    - A universal masters-only load into a stepped engine keeps
    `safe_get_full_optimizer_state` and `safe_set_full_optimizer_state`
    working.
    - A pipeline-serialized load with missing shards raises before
    `dist.recv`. The NVMe masters-only copy restores only the fp32 swap
    file.
    - [x] 4×H200, torch 2.9.1+cu130, Python 3.12.12, same two files on tree
    `a22f0cc4`: 10 passed in 52s. This includes the three data-parallel
    change tests (universal, legacy, elastic), which spawn 2 ranks on
    `cuda:0`/`cuda:1`. The #8891 suite there does not cover these two
    optimizers.
    
    Validated cells: dedicated ZeRO-1 BF16 optimizer and ZeRO-3, same
    data-parallel size, legacy checkpoint, bf16, no offload. ZeRO-1/2
    universal masters-only load covered by the fragment test. Open cells:
    fp16, MoE, real NVMe offload (the NVMe test uses a stub swapper), and a
    data-parallel size change.
    
    ---------
    
    Signed-off-by: Olatunji Ruwase <tunji.ruwase@snowflake.com>
    Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commit a7ebdf96f062461af2073f7c7b93d5e1febe39f0
Author: 0z5a <dezhen.lu@student.uni-tuebingen.de>
Date:   Sat Nov 7 15:56:22 2026 +0000

    Fix routed-expert gradient clipping for AutoEP + AutoTP folding (#8823)
    
    AutoEP + AutoTP folding gives TP peers different routed experts.
    ZeRO-1/2 currently filters non-TP expert parameters to TP rank zero when
    computing the clipping norm, then applies the ordinary expert-norm
    averaging path. This can omit expert owners and produce an incorrect
    clipping coefficient even when reconstructed logical gradients are
    correct.
    
    Compute folded expert norms over the actual expert-DP partition group
    and EP owner group, without another TP sum or expert-norm average. Only
    groups tagged with the AutoEP expert placement family use this path.
    Dense groups and native MoE groups retain their existing reductions and
    native expert-norm averaging, including when native ETP and AutoEP
    groups coexist. ZeRO-3 is unchanged and is checked as a sibling
    reference. The existing folding contract rejects optimizer/parameter
    offload.
    
    Refs #8672 and #8670. The live duplicate check found no open PR fixing
    this ZeRO-1/2 folding path. #8476, #8478 and #8691 address FP32/ZeRO-0
    clipping in `runtime/utils.py`; they do not change the partitioned
    optimizer reductions fixed here. #8739 implements DeepEP weight-gradient
    overlap and does not change these norm reductions.
    
    ### Final change
    
    This PR contains three files:
    
    - `deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage_1_and_2.py`: correct the folded expert
    clipping reductions.
    - `tests/unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_autotp_sharded_attention.py`:
    reconstruct full logical gradients and FP32 master parameters, then
    compare an actual SGD update against an unsharded ZeRO-0 reference
    across all 45 parameter families. Thresholds of 0.5 and 2.0 times the
    reference norm cover active clipping and an inactive control. Snapshots
    are cloned before in-place updates; distributed diagnostics finish
    before assertions.
    - `docs/code-docs/source/autoep.rst`: document expert ownership and the
    reduction contract.
    
    The sharded-attention regression supports 4- and 8-rank TP2/EP4
    configurations, ZeRO-1/2/3 and ZeRO-3 `zero.Init`. An additional
    two-rank analytic SGD regression covers native ETP alone and mixed
    native ETP/folded AutoEP groups at ZeRO-1/2.
    
    ### Incremental review
    
    [Incremental review report and
    validation](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/pull/8823#issuecomment-6175700151)
    · [diff from the reviewed
    head](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/compare/352ee55cd14f77f30e5170939c7e60c4d4bd7754...fb5d0e5efa6d9aec89b26cd022e50d4862478945).
    
    The correction preserves native ETP reductions alongside folded AutoEP.
    **On the correction commit, 8 positive cases passed on 2 H100 GPUs, and
    2 published-head negative controls failed as expected.** ZeRO-1/2
    optimizer cases validate native norm 5, mixed norm 13 and the actual
    clipped-SGD updates; TP2/EP2 tiny GLM4-MoE active/inactive clipping
    cases validate all 45 parameter families against an unsharded reference.
    The old mixed cases produce partial norms 12.369317 / 12.649111 instead
    of 13. These runs used FP32, TF32 disabled, Torch 2.12.1+cu130 / CUDA
    13.0, Transformers 5.15.1 and driver 595.91.07. Changed-file pre-commit
    checks and independent archive/report readback passed; owned workers and
    locks closed. The report records the exact execution method and CPU
    diagnostic separately. The 8/16-GPU results below belong to the original
    submitted head.
    
    ### Original submitted-head validation
    
    The original submitted three-file diff at
    `352ee55cd14f77f30e5170939c7e60c4d4bd7754` was tested on source based on
    `1c862f7df93f0345b977c67f5408d967b94bf4ae`. The extended finite workload
    used **16 NVIDIA H100 GPUs across four nodes**, random tiny GLM4-MoE,
    FP32 with TF32 disabled, Torch 2.12.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0 and Transformers
    5.15.1. The original receipt did not capture the NVML driver package
    version.
    
    | Coverage | Final result |
    |---|---|
    | Clipping and initialization | TP2/EP4 and TP2/EP8, ZeRO-1/2/3,
    active/inactive clipping and ZeRO-3 `zero.Init` passed. An unfixed
    ZeRO-2 control failed the norm/update oracle. |
    | Routing and topology | Rotating hotspots, idle expert owners, GAS4,
    and TP4/EP16 with 16 experts and ZeRO-3 `zero.Init` passed. |
    | Communication | Overlap off/on and small-bucket configurations with
    actual repeated/oversize flushes passed. |
    | Save and resume | Continuous four-update training matched save after
    two updates, process exit and new-process resume through four updates,
    including parameters, momentum 0.9, losses and WarmupLR state. |
    | Sustained training | 200 actual updates across four 50-update routing
    stages passed the reference loss, gradient and update checks. Late live
    allocated-memory spread stayed below 64 MiB for this tiny model. |
    | Independent readback | All 28 cases, 448 rank packets and 247,635 raw
    arrays from the 16-GPU workloads passed separate NumPy arithmetic and
    complete archive checksum verification. |
    | Source checks | All applicable changed-files pre-commit hooks passed,
    including yapf, flake8, codespell, license and accelerator/distributed
    import checks. `git diff --check` and a clean three-way merge check
    against current upstream master passed. |
    
    The extended distributed drivers used the same contributed reference
    helpers. An additional 8-H100 clipping matrix passed 16 cases and 28,800
    raw arrays. All owned GPU workers and contexts closed, the original GPU
    locks were released, and complete outputs were archived.
    
    Idle-owner checks exclude alignment padding using the frozen permutation
    formula `ceil((n_tokens + E_local*8)/8)*8`; equality to `E_local*8`
    proves zero actual received rows. The original finalizer's incorrect
    padding assertion and failed scheduler status are preserved in the
    private evidence. The separate corrected reader passed against the same
    completed workload and unchanged numerical tolerances.
    
    These results establish tiny-model correctness, optimizer-state
    continuity and bounded-run stability. They do not establish
    pretrained-model convergence, a speedup, BF16/FP16 or Muon behavior,
    offload, PP/SP, DeepEP overlap, or completion of every Q4 roadmap item.
    
    Reproduce the contributed regression and source checks:
    
    ```sh
    pytest --forked -q tests/unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_autotp_sharded_attention.py \
      -k TestShardedAttentionClippedUpdate
    pre-commit run --files deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage_1_and_2.py \
      tests/unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_autotp_sharded_attention.py \
      docs/code-docs/source/autoep.rst
    ```
    
    AI assistance was used for implementation, test preparation and
    incremental review. The human submitter reviewed the original
    submission, confirmed its test results, and authorized this follow-up
    correction and DCO sign-off.
    
    ---------
    
    Signed-off-by: 0z5a <dezhen.lu@student.uni-tuebingen.de>
    Co-authored-by: pengdurice <pengduhit@gmail.com>

Author: 0z5a <dezhen.lu@student.uni-tuebingen.de>

    Fix routed-expert gradient clipping for AutoEP + AutoTP folding (#8823)
    
    AutoEP + AutoTP folding gives TP peers different routed experts.
    ZeRO-1/2 currently filters non-TP expert parameters to TP rank zero when
    computing the clipping norm, then applies the ordinary expert-norm
    averaging path. This can omit expert owners and produce an incorrect
    clipping coefficient even when reconstructed logical gradients are
    correct.
    
    Compute folded expert norms over the actual expert-DP partition group
    and EP owner group, without another TP sum or expert-norm average. Only
    groups tagged with the AutoEP expert placement family use this path.
    Dense groups and native MoE groups retain their existing reductions and
    native expert-norm averaging, including when native ETP and AutoEP
    groups coexist. ZeRO-3 is unchanged and is checked as a sibling
    reference. The existing folding contract rejects optimizer/parameter
    offload.
    
    Refs #8672 and #8670. The live duplicate check found no open PR fixing
    this ZeRO-1/2 folding path. #8476, #8478 and #8691 address FP32/ZeRO-0
    clipping in `runtime/utils.py`; they do not change the partitioned
    optimizer reductions fixed here. #8739 implements DeepEP weight-gradient
    overlap and does not change these norm reductions.
    
    ### Final change
    
    This PR contains three files:
    
    - `deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage_1_and_2.py`: correct the folded expert
    clipping reductions.
    - `tests/unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_autotp_sharded_attention.py`:
    reconstruct full logical gradients and FP32 master parameters, then
    compare an actual SGD update against an unsharded ZeRO-0 reference
    across all 45 parameter families. Thresholds of 0.5 and 2.0 times the
    reference norm cover active clipping and an inactive control. Snapshots
    are cloned before in-place updates; distributed diagnostics finish
    before assertions.
    - `docs/code-docs/source/autoep.rst`: document expert ownership and the
    reduction contract.
    
    The sharded-attention regression supports 4- and 8-rank TP2/EP4
    configurations, ZeRO-1/2/3 and ZeRO-3 `zero.Init`. An additional
    two-rank analytic SGD regression covers native ETP alone and mixed
    native ETP/folded AutoEP groups at ZeRO-1/2.
    
    ### Incremental review
    
    [Incremental review report and
    validation](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/pull/8823#issuecomment-6175700151)
    · [diff from the reviewed
    head](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/compare/352ee55cd14f77f30e5170939c7e60c4d4bd7754...fb5d0e5efa6d9aec89b26cd022e50d4862478945).
    
    The correction preserves native ETP reductions alongside folded AutoEP.
    **On the correction commit, 8 positive cases passed on 2 H100 GPUs, and
    2 published-head negative controls failed as expected.** ZeRO-1/2
    optimizer cases validate native norm 5, mixed norm 13 and the actual
    clipped-SGD updates; TP2/EP2 tiny GLM4-MoE active/inactive clipping
    cases validate all 45 parameter families against an unsharded reference.
    The old mixed cases produce partial norms 12.369317 / 12.649111 instead
    of 13. These runs used FP32, TF32 disabled, Torch 2.12.1+cu130 / CUDA
    13.0, Transformers 5.15.1 and driver 595.91.07. Changed-file pre-commit
    checks and independent archive/report readback passed; owned workers and
    locks closed. The report records the exact execution method and CPU
    diagnostic separately. The 8/16-GPU results below belong to the original
    submitted head.
    
    ### Original submitted-head validation
    
    The original submitted three-file diff at
    `352ee55cd14f77f30e5170939c7e60c4d4bd7754` was tested on source based on
    `1c862f7df93f0345b977c67f5408d967b94bf4ae`. The extended finite workload
    used **16 NVIDIA H100 GPUs across four nodes**, random tiny GLM4-MoE,
    FP32 with TF32 disabled, Torch 2.12.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0 and Transformers
    5.15.1. The original receipt did not capture the NVML driver package
    version.

    | Sustained training | 200 actual updates across four 50-update routing

    AutoEP + AutoTP folding gives TP peers different routed experts.
    ZeRO-1/2 currently filters non-TP expert parameters to TP rank zero when
    computing the clipping norm, then applies the ordinary expert-norm
    averaging path. This can omit expert owners and produce an incorrect
    clipping coefficient even when reconstructed logical gradients are
    correct.
    
    Compute folded expert norms over the actual expert-DP partition group
    and EP owner group, without another TP sum or expert-norm average. Only
    groups tagged with the AutoEP expert placement family use this path.
    Dense groups and native MoE groups retain their existing reductions and
    native expert-norm averaging, including when native ETP and AutoEP
    groups coexist. ZeRO-3 is unchanged and is checked as a sibling
    reference. The existing folding contract rejects optimizer/parameter
    offload.
    
    Refs #8672 and #8670. The live duplicate check found no open PR fixing
    this ZeRO-1/2 folding path. #8476, #8478 and #8691 address FP32/ZeRO-0
    clipping in `runtime/utils.py`; they do not change the partitioned
    optimizer reductions fixed here. #8739 implements DeepEP weight-gradient
    overlap and does not change these norm reductions.

    This PR contains three files:
    
    - `deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage_1_and_2.py`: correct the folded expert
    clipping reductions.
    - `tests/unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_autotp_sharded_attention.py`:
    reconstruct full logical gradients and FP32 master parameters, then
    compare an actual SGD update against an unsharded ZeRO-0 reference
    across all 45 parameter families. Thresholds of 0.5 and 2.0 times the
    reference norm cover active clipping and an inactive control. Snapshots
    are cloned before in-place updates; distributed diagnostics finish
    before assertions.
    - `docs/code-docs/source/autoep.rst`: document expert ownership and the
    reduction contract.
    
    The sharded-attention regression supports 4- and 8-rank TP2/EP4
    configurations, ZeRO-1/2/3 and ZeRO-3 `zero.Init`. An additional
    two-rank analytic SGD regression covers native ETP alone and mixed
    native ETP/folded AutoEP groups at ZeRO-1/2.

    [Incremental review report and
    validation](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/pull/8823#issuecomment-6175700151)

    optimizer cases validate native norm 5, mixed norm 13 and the actual

    submitted head.

Author: William Yao <143197278+anyadontfly@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Sun Nov 8 08:29:38 2026 +0000

    feat(rollout): non-greedy sampling on hybrid engine graph decode path (#8939)
    
    Closes #8934.
    
    ## Summary
    
    `HybridEngineRollout` decodes greedily on its fast paths. Graph capture
    applies only when `temperature <= 0`, and sampling silently falls back
    to Hugging Face `generate()`. Continuous batching (#8368), with or
    without its CUDA graph (#8732), rejects `temperature > 0` outright. RL
    rollouts sample at temperature 1, so they get neither path.
    
    Only the decode forward is captured; the next token is picked on the
    host from the output logits. So sampling needs no change to any captured
    graph. This PR changes token selection and dispatch only:
    
    - **One token selector**,
    `HybridEngineRollout._token_selector(sampling)`, picks the first token
    and every decoded token on all three paths: graph decode, continuous
    batching, and continuous batching with graphs.
      - At `temperature <= 0` it takes the argmax, as before.
    - Otherwise it applies Hugging Face's `TemperatureLogitsWarper`,
    `TopKLogitsWarper` and `TopPLogitsWarper`, in `generate()`'s order on
    float32 logits, then calls `torch.multinomial`. So every path samples
    from the same distribution as `generate()`.
    - **Graph dispatch:** sampled requests go to the graph path;
    `generate()` no longer checks `is_greedy` for it.
    - **Continuous batching:**
      - The greedy-only check is removed.
    - The model's repetition penalty is applied before the selector, which
    is `generate()`'s order.
    - **`_hf_sampling_kwargs(sampling)`:** the `generate()` sampling
    arguments, now shared by the main `generate()` call and the
    continuous-batching prefill of models without cache-class support. That
    prefill previously hard-coded `do_sample=False`.
    - **Docs:** `inference-engine.rst` now describes sampling on the graph
    decode path, and "greedy decoding" is dropped from the continuous
    batching requirements.
    
    ## Known issues outside this PR
    
    On master, two cache and mask gaps stop some paths from running on a
    Hugging Face model with SDPA attention, greedy included. This PR doesn't
    touch either; #8602 fixes both.
    - **Plain graph path (`_generate_graph`), Transformers 4.57.x:** capture
    fails with "operation not permitted when stream is capturing". The
    decode step's 2-D attention mask makes Transformers call
    `padding_mask.all()` on the host (reported by 0z5a on #8197). #8602
    passes a pre-built 4-D decode mask.
    - **Plain graph path and continuous batching without graphs,
    Transformers 5.x:** `DeepSpeedStaticCache` has no `get_query_offset`
    (also #8852). #8602 adds it.
    
    Until #8602 lands, the end-to-end GPU tests of these paths fail with
    those errors (results below).
    
    ## Tests
    
    The tests cover correct dispatch and correct sampling.
    
    `tests/unit/runtime/rollout/test_hybrid_engine_rollout.py` (CPU):
    - The graph dispatch test also runs at temperature 0.7 and checks that
    `generate()` is not called.
    - `test_token_selector_samples_the_configured_distribution`: 20,000
    draws from fixed logits for temperature, top-k, top-p and their
    combination. They are compared against a reference distribution computed
    independently of the rollout. No token outside the top-k / top-p support
    may appear, and every token's frequency must lie within 4 standard
    errors.
    - `test_token_selector_is_argmax_without_temperature`.
    - `test_continuous_generation_samples_when_temperature_is_set`:
    - setup: continuous batching on a fake model whose logits tie tokens 7
    and 8, with top-k 2;
    - check: the output must contain both tokens and nothing else (greedy
    would always pick 7);
    - this replaces the assertion that continuous batching rejects
    `temperature > 0`.
    - `test_continuous_sampling_applies_repetition_penalty_before_warpers`:
    with penalty 1.5 and top-k 1, the token the penalty favors must win.
    
    `tests/unit/v1/test_hybrid_engine_rollout_v1.py` (CUDA):
    `test_decode_sampling_matches_hf_generate` samples end to end on a tiny
    random Llama, with a scaled output head so next-token distributions are
    peaked.
    - Paths: graph decode, continuous batching, and continuous batching with
    graphs.
    - Settings: (temperature 1), (temperature 0.7, top-k 5) and (temperature
    1, top-p 0.8).
    - Check: under the same seed, the generated tokens must equal Hugging
    Face `generate()`'s exactly. Every prompt gets its own continuous
    batching slot, so each path draws all rows' tokens in one call per step,
    as `generate()` does, and both consume the same random numbers.
    
    Results on this branch (master `322283b25` + this PR), 1× NVIDIA A40
    (driver 595.71.05), torch 2.14.1+cu130:
    
    | Transformers | Result | Failures |
    |---|---|---|
    | 4.57.1 | 91 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped | the 3 plain graph-path
    cases: capture error (`padding_mask.all()`) |
    | 5.19.0 | 88 passed, 6 failed, 1 skipped | the 3 plain graph-path and 3
    continuous-batching-without-graphs cases: no `get_query_offset` |
    
    All failures are the master issues above, which #8602 fixes. Every CPU
    test passes on both versions, and so does continuous batching with
    graphs end to end. The skipped test is the optional pretrained-model
    test
    (`DEEPSPEED_PRETRAINED_ROLLOUT_MODEL`).
    
    ---------
    
    Signed-off-by: Puyuan Yao <williamyao034@gmail.com>
    Co-authored-by: Ma, Guokai <guokai.ma@gmail.com>

    Closes #8934.
    
    ## Summary
    
    `HybridEngineRollout` decodes greedily on its fast paths. Graph capture
    applies only when `temperature <= 0`, and sampling silently falls back
    to Hugging Face `generate()`. Continuous batching (#8368), with or
    without its CUDA graph (#8732), rejects `temperature > 0` outright. RL
    rollouts sample at temperature 1, so they get neither path.
    
    Only the decode forward is captured; the next token is picked on the
    host from the output logits. So sampling needs no change to any captured
    graph. This PR changes token selection and dispatch only:
    
    - **One token selector**,
    `HybridEngineRollout._token_selector(sampling)`, picks the first token
    and every decoded token on all three paths: graph decode, continuous
    batching, and continuous batching with graphs.
      - At `temperature <= 0` it takes the argmax, as before.
    - Otherwise it applies Hugging Face's `TemperatureLogitsWarper`,
    `TopKLogitsWarper` and `TopPLogitsWarper`, in `generate()`'s order on
    float32 logits, then calls `torch.multinomial`. So every path samples
    from the same distribution as `generate()`.
    - **Graph dispatch:** sampled requests go to the graph path;
    `generate()` no longer checks `is_greedy` for it.
    - **Continuous batching:**
      - The greedy-only check is removed.
    - The model's repetition penalty is applied before the selector, which
    is `generate()`'s order.
    - **`_hf_sampling_kwargs(sampling)`:** the `generate()` sampling
    arguments, now shared by the main `generate()` call and the
    continuous-batching prefill of models without cache-class support. That
    prefill previously hard-coded `do_sample=False`.
    - **Docs:** `inference-engine.rst` now describes sampling on the graph
    decode path, and "greedy decoding" is dropped from the continuous
    batching requirements.

    On master, two cache and mask gaps stop some paths from running on a
    Hugging Face model with SDPA attention, greedy included. This PR doesn't
    touch either; #8602 fixes both.
    - **Plain graph path (`_generate_graph`), Transformers 4.57.x:** capture
    fails with "operation not permitted when stream is capturing". The
    decode step's 2-D attention mask makes Transformers call
    `padding_mask.all()` on the host (reported by 0z5a on #8197). #8602
    passes a pre-built 4-D decode mask.
    - **Plain graph path and continuous batching without graphs,
    Transformers 5.x:** `DeepSpeedStaticCache` has no `get_query_offset`
    (also #8852). #8602 adds it.

    those errors (results below).

    - The graph dispatch test also runs at temperature 0.7 and checks that
    `generate()` is not called.

    draws from fixed logits for temperature, top-k, top-p and their
    combination. They are compared against a reference distribution computed
    independently of the rollout. No token outside the top-k / top-p support
    may appear, and every token's frequency must lie within 4 standard
    errors.

    would always pick 7);

    `temperature > 0`.

    with penalty 1.5 and top-k 1, the token the penalty favors must win.

    peaked.

    continuous-batching-without-graphs cases: no `get_query_offset` |

    test passes on both versions, and so does continuous batching with
    graphs end to end. The skipped test is the optional pretrained-model
    test

Author: Xinyu Lian <lian7@illinois.edu>

    ZeRO-3 NVMe offload: fix "param already assigned swap buffer" in the parameter prefetch (#9014)
    
    ## Summary
    
    With `offload_param: {device: nvme}`, training fails from the second
    step on with `AssertionError: param N already assigned swap buffer id M`
    (#4072, open since 2023, reported with HF gradient checkpointing).
    
    The parameter trace has an entry per use. The NVMe prefetch
    (`__prefetch_nvme_param_partitions`) collects every parameter in its
    window that is still on NVMe, so a parameter used twice in the window
    goes to `swap_in()` twice: the last layer for the forward and again for
    the backward, or a checkpointed layer for its recompute and again for
    its backward. `swap_in()` then asserts on the second buffer. The
    all-gather prefetch above it already skips duplicates; this PR does the
    same in the NVMe prefetch.
    
    A parameter is used twice within the window when:
    - it is in one of the last layers: their forward is followed directly by
    their backward;
    - it is in a checkpointed layer: the layer runs its forward again right
    before its backward (the #4072 case);
    - its layer is applied twice in a row in one forward, e.g. a shared
    layer.
    
    Signed-off-by: Xinyu Lian <lian7@illinois.edu>

    same in the NVMe prefetch.

    their backward;
    - it is in a checkpointed layer: the layer runs its forward again right
    before its backward (the #4072 case);
    - its layer is applied twice in a row in one forward, e.g. a shared
    layer.

commit 02f7978481cb3d3297f111c02b16d768b890b256
Author: William Yao <143197278+anyadontfly@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Sun Nov 8 08:29:38 2026 +0000

    feat(rollout): non-greedy sampling on hybrid engine graph decode path (#8939)
    
    Closes #8934.
    
    ## Summary
    
    `HybridEngineRollout` decodes greedily on its fast paths. Graph capture
    applies only when `temperature <= 0`, and sampling silently falls back
    to Hugging Face `generate()`. Continuous batching (#8368), with or
    without its CUDA graph (#8732), rejects `temperature > 0` outright. RL
    rollouts sample at temperature 1, so they get neither path.
    
    Only the decode forward is captured; the next token is picked on the
    host from the output logits. So sampling needs no change to any captured
    graph. This PR changes token selection and dispatch only:
    
    - **One token selector**,
    `HybridEngineRollout._token_selector(sampling)`, picks the first token
    and every decoded token on all three paths: graph decode, continuous
    batching, and continuous batching with graphs.
      - At `temperature <= 0` it takes the argmax, as before.
    - Otherwise it applies Hugging Face's `TemperatureLogitsWarper`,
    `TopKLogitsWarper` and `TopPLogitsWarper`, in `generate()`'s order on
    float32 logits, then calls `torch.multinomial`. So every path samples
    from the same distribution as `generate()`.
    - **Graph dispatch:** sampled requests go to the graph path;
    `generate()` no longer checks `is_greedy` for it.
    - **Continuous batching:**
      - The greedy-only check is removed.
    - The model's repetition penalty is applied before the selector, which
    is `generate()`'s order.
    - **`_hf_sampling_kwargs(sampling)`:** the `generate()` sampling
    arguments, now shared by the main `generate()` call and the
    continuous-batching prefill of models without cache-class support. That
    prefill previously hard-coded `do_sample=False`.
    - **Docs:** `inference-engine.rst` now describes sampling on the graph
    decode path, and "greedy decoding" is dropped from the continuous
    batching requirements.
    
    ## Known issues outside this PR
    
    On master, two cache and mask gaps stop some paths from running on a
    Hugging Face model with SDPA attention, greedy included. This PR doesn't
    touch either; #8602 fixes both.
    - **Plain graph path (`_generate_graph`), Transformers 4.57.x:** capture
    fails with "operation not permitted when stream is capturing". The
    decode step's 2-D attention mask makes Transformers call
    `padding_mask.all()` on the host (reported by 0z5a on #8197). #8602
    passes a pre-built 4-D decode mask.
    - **Plain graph path and continuous batching without graphs,
    Transformers 5.x:** `DeepSpeedStaticCache` has no `get_query_offset`
    (also #8852). #8602 adds it.
    
    Until #8602 lands, the end-to-end GPU tests of these paths fail with
    those errors (results below).
    
    ## Tests
    
    The tests cover correct dispatch and correct sampling.
    
    `tests/unit/runtime/rollout/test_hybrid_engine_rollout.py` (CPU):
    - The graph dispatch test also runs at temperature 0.7 and checks that
    `generate()` is not called.
    - `test_token_selector_samples_the_configured_distribution`: 20,000
    draws from fixed logits for temperature, top-k, top-p and their
    combination. They are compared against a reference distribution computed
    independently of the rollout. No token outside the top-k / top-p support
    may appear, and every token's frequency must lie within 4 standard
    errors.
    - `test_token_selector_is_argmax_without_temperature`.
    - `test_continuous_generation_samples_when_temperature_is_set`:
    - setup: continuous batching on a fake model whose logits tie tokens 7
    and 8, with top-k 2;
    - check: the output must contain both tokens and nothing else (greedy
    would always pick 7);
    - this replaces the assertion that continuous batching rejects
    `temperature > 0`.
    - `test_continuous_sampling_applies_repetition_penalty_before_warpers`:
    with penalty 1.5 and top-k 1, the token the penalty favors must win.
    
    `tests/unit/v1/test_hybrid_engine_rollout_v1.py` (CUDA):
    `test_decode_sampling_matches_hf_generate` samples end to end on a tiny
    random Llama, with a scaled output head so next-token distributions are
    peaked.
    - Paths: graph decode, continuous batching, and continuous batching with
    graphs.
    - Settings: (temperature 1), (temperature 0.7, top-k 5) and (temperature
    1, top-p 0.8).
    - Check: under the same seed, the generated tokens must equal Hugging
    Face `generate()`'s exactly. Every prompt gets its own continuous
    batching slot, so each path draws all rows' tokens in one call per step,
    as `generate()` does, and both consume the same random numbers.
    
    Results on this branch (master `322283b25` + this PR), 1× NVIDIA A40
    (driver 595.71.05), torch 2.14.1+cu130:
    
    | Transformers | Result | Failures |
    |---|---|---|
    | 4.57.1 | 91 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped | the 3 plain graph-path
    cases: capture error (`padding_mask.all()`) |
    | 5.19.0 | 88 passed, 6 failed, 1 skipped | the 3 plain graph-path and 3
    continuous-batching-without-graphs cases: no `get_query_offset` |
    
    All failures are the master issues above, which #8602 fixes. Every CPU
    test passes on both versions, and so does continuous batching with
    graphs end to end. The skipped test is the optional pretrained-model
    test
    (`DEEPSPEED_PRETRAINED_ROLLOUT_MODEL`).
    
    ---------
    
    Signed-off-by: Puyuan Yao <williamyao034@gmail.com>
    Co-authored-by: Ma, Guokai <guokai.ma@gmail.com>

Author: pengdurice <pengduhit@gmail.com>
Date:   Sat Nov 7 05:43:45 2026 +0000

    AutoEP: read and write the transformers output-capture registry as a dict (#9029)
    
    ## AutoEP: read and write the transformers output-capture registry as a
    dict
    
    ### Problem
    
    `cpu-torch-latest` installs transformers from git `main`, and since
    2026-11-06 it fails on every PR with:
    
    ```
    FAILED unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_unit.py::TestModelDetectionAndReplacement::test_hf_mixtral_causal_lm_matches_autoep_with_router_logits
    FAILED unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_unit.py::TestModelDetectionAndReplacement::test_hf_minimax_m3_causal_lm_matches_autoep_with_router_logits
    E       TypeError: _CanRecordRegistry.get() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given
    deepspeed/module_inject/auto_ep_presets/base.py:326
    ```
    
    ### Cause
    
    huggingface/transformers#49594 (commit `c5bd76ec51`, 2026-11-06) changed
    `transformers.utils.output_capturing._CAN_RECORD_REGISTRY` from a plain
    dict to `class _CanRecordRegistry(dict)`, whose `get(model)` and
    `__setitem__(model, value)` take a model and use `str(model.__class__)`
    as the key. The released transformers 5.22.1 and 5.22.2 still have the
    plain dict.
    
    AutoEP's `router_logits` retargeting
    (`deepspeed/module_inject/auto_ep_presets/base.py`) uses the registry as
    a plain dict keyed by `str(module.__class__)`:
    
    | Line | Call | With the new class |
    |---|---|---|
    | 326 | `registry.get(key, default)` | `TypeError` (the failure above) |
    | 364 | `registry.get(key)` | looks up `"<class 'str'>"` and returns
    `{}` |
    | 305 | `registry[key] = entry` (restore) | stores under `"<class
    'str'>"` |
    
    `registry.pop` and `registry.update` are not overridden and keep
    working.
    
    ### Change
    
    | Where | What |
    |---|---|
    | `deepspeed/module_inject/auto_ep_presets/base.py` | Two helpers,
    `_registry_get` and `_registry_set`, call `dict.get` and
    `dict.__setitem__` directly; lines 305, 326 and 364 use them. The keys
    stay `str(module.__class__)`, which is also what the subclass stores
    under, so this works for both registry shapes. |
    | `tests/unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_unit.py` |
    `TestTransformersOutputRecorderRegistry`: runs
    `_install_instance_transformers_output_recorders` with a plain dict and
    with a dict subclass that mirrors the new `get(model)` /
    `__setitem__(model, value)`; checks that the retargeted entries are
    visible under the class key while the hooks are installed, and that the
    registry is restored exactly afterwards (the original entry back, the
    added one removed). CI runs one transformers version, so this covers
    both shapes in every run. |
    
    ### Duplicate check
    
    Searched open PRs and issues on 2026-11-06 for "_CanRecordRegistry",
    "_CAN_RECORD_REGISTRY", "output capture registry" and the error message:
    none found.
    
    ### Tests
    
    Hardware: CPU only (`DS_ACCELERATOR=cpu`), Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C,
    Ubuntu 22.04.5, CPython 3.12.14, torch 2.10.0, pytest 8.3.5,
    pytest-xdist 3.8.0. Command, from `tests/`: `pytest --forked -n 4
    unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_unit.py` (as in `cpu-torch-latest`).
    
    | `unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_unit.py` | transformers 5.22.1 (plain dict) |
    transformers `main` at `073a202c6` (`_CanRecordRegistry`) |
    |---|---|---|
    | master (`8af59b2e7`) | 197 passed, 6 skipped | 2 failed (the two tests
    above), 195 passed, 6 skipped |
    | this PR | 199 passed, 6 skipped | 199 passed, 6 skipped |
    | the new test on master's code | `plain_dict` passes, `model_keyed`
    fails | `plain_dict` passes, `model_keyed` fails |
    
    `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files: all hooks pass.
    
    Not run: GPU (the change touches only registry reads and writes on the
    host).
    
    ### Compatibility
    
    AutoEP with Hugging Face models that record `router_logits`: the
    Mixtral, MiniMax-M3 and Qwen3-MoE presets (through
    `TransformersTopLevelRouterLogitsAdapter`) and the Qwen3.5-MoE preset
    use this path. Works with transformers 5.22.x and with transformers
    `main`. No ZeRO, offload, precision or parallelism behavior changes.
    
    ### AI assistance
    
    This change, its test and this description were prepared with AI
    assistance (Claude), which also ran the tests above.

    Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit 1b022dcd4d45782f0af5b106cb3a2b2ca1092e16
Author: Xinyu Lian <lian7@illinois.edu>
Date:   Sat Nov 7 08:48:22 2026 +0000

    DeepNVMe: fix silent I/O failures on misaligned buffers (#8985)
    
    ## Summary
    
    DeepNVMe does not check the result of an I/O request, so a request that
    the kernel fails is reported as done. ZeRO-Infinity reads and writes
    views into flat buffers at offsets that are often not 512-byte aligned,
    and O_DIRECT fails those on md RAID, LVM, and before Linux 6.0 on every
    block device. Swap-ins then leave stale data, swap-outs write nothing,
    and training goes on with wrong weights and gradients.
    
    This PR checks every completed request: a failed op makes `wait()`,
    `sync_pread()` and `sync_pwrite()` raise `RuntimeError` after the other
    ops complete. Tensors that are not contiguous, or not aligned as the
    file needs (`statx`, else 512), go through the existing bounce buffer.
    ZeRO-Infinity's fast init reads partitions of unaligned length through a
    padded staging tensor. Also, `io_submit` errors no longer abort on an
    assert, `io_pgetevents` is retried after `EINTR`, and a failed
    `io_queue_init` raises.
    
    ## Fixes
    
    Before → after, GH200, ext4 on md RAID 0, base `1a956270f`:
    
    1. I/O on a pinned view 416 bytes past an aligned address: nothing
    moved, success returned → data moved.
    2. ZeRO-3, NVMe parameter offload, Qwen2.5-0.5B: 60 of 290 parameters
    wrong after `initialize` → 0; the first loss now equals CPU offload's
    (12.206690).
    3. ZeRO-3, NVMe optimizer offload, 2 ranks, Qwen2.5 config: losses leave
    CPU offload's at step 2 → equal.
    4. A write past the file size limit: success with 2048 of 4096 bytes on
    disk → `RuntimeError: ... File too large`.
    5. A write to a read-only file, or a signal to an AIO thread during a
    read: the process aborts on an `assert` → `RuntimeError: ... Bad file
    descriptor`, or the read completes.
    
    ---------
    
    Signed-off-by: Xinyu Lian <lian7@illinois.edu>
    Co-authored-by: Olatunji Ruwase <tunji.ruwase@snowflake.com>

commit 1b022dcd4d45782f0af5b106cb3a2b2ca1092e16
Author: Xinyu Lian <lian7@illinois.edu>
Date:   Sat Nov 7 08:48:22 2026 +0000

    DeepNVMe: fix silent I/O failures on misaligned buffers (#8985)
    
    ## Summary
    
    DeepNVMe does not check the result of an I/O request, so a request that
    the kernel fails is reported as done. ZeRO-Infinity reads and writes
    views into flat buffers at offsets that are often not 512-byte aligned,
    and O_DIRECT fails those on md RAID, LVM, and before Linux 6.0 on every
    block device. Swap-ins then leave stale data, swap-outs write nothing,
    and training goes on with wrong weights and gradients.
    
    This PR checks every completed request: a failed op makes `wait()`,
    `sync_pread()` and `sync_pwrite()` raise `RuntimeError` after the other
    ops complete. Tensors that are not contiguous, or not aligned as the
    file needs (`statx`, else 512), go through the existing bounce buffer.
    ZeRO-Infinity's fast init reads partitions of unaligned length through a
    padded staging tensor. Also, `io_submit` errors no longer abort on an
    assert, `io_pgetevents` is retried after `EINTR`, and a failed
    `io_queue_init` raises.
    
    ## Fixes
    
    Before → after, GH200, ext4 on md RAID 0, base `1a956270f`:
    
    1. I/O on a pinned view 416 bytes past an aligned address: nothing
    moved, success returned → data moved.
    2. ZeRO-3, NVMe parameter offload, Qwen2.5-0.5B: 60 of 290 parameters
    wrong after `initialize` → 0; the first loss now equals CPU offload's
    (12.206690).
    3. ZeRO-3, NVMe optimizer offload, 2 ranks, Qwen2.5 config: losses leave
    CPU offload's at step 2 → equal.
    4. A write past the file size limit: success with 2048 of 4096 bytes on
    disk → `RuntimeError: ... File too large`.
    5. A write to a read-only file, or a signal to an AIO thread during a
    read: the process aborts on an `assert` → `RuntimeError: ... Bad file
    descriptor`, or the read completes.
    
    ---------
    
    Signed-off-by: Xinyu Lian <lian7@illinois.edu>
    Co-authored-by: Olatunji Ruwase <tunji.ruwase@snowflake.com>

    DeepNVMe: fix silent I/O failures on misaligned buffers (#8985)
    
    ## Summary
    
    DeepNVMe does not check the result of an I/O request, so a request that
    the kernel fails is reported as done. ZeRO-Infinity reads and writes
    views into flat buffers at offsets that are often not 512-byte aligned,
    and O_DIRECT fails those on md RAID, LVM, and before Linux 6.0 on every
    block device. Swap-ins then leave stale data, swap-outs write nothing,
    and training goes on with wrong weights and gradients.
    
    This PR checks every completed request: a failed op makes `wait()`,
    `sync_pread()` and `sync_pwrite()` raise `RuntimeError` after the other
    ops complete. Tensors that are not contiguous, or not aligned as the
    file needs (`statx`, else 512), go through the existing bounce buffer.
    ZeRO-Infinity's fast init reads partitions of unaligned length through a
    padded staging tensor. Also, `io_submit` errors no longer abort on an
    assert, `io_pgetevents` is retried after `EINTR`, and a failed
    `io_queue_init` raises.
    
    ## Fixes
    
    Before → after, GH200, ext4 on md RAID 0, base `1a956270f`:
    
    1. I/O on a pinned view 416 bytes past an aligned address: nothing
    moved, success returned → data moved.
    2. ZeRO-3, NVMe parameter offload, Qwen2.5-0.5B: 60 of 290 parameters
    wrong after `initialize` → 0; the first loss now equals CPU offload's
    (12.206690).
    3. ZeRO-3, NVMe optimizer offload, 2 ranks, Qwen2.5 config: losses leave
    CPU offload's at step 2 → equal.
    4. A write past the file size limit: success with 2048 of 4096 bytes on
    disk → `RuntimeError: ... File too large`.
    5. A write to a read-only file, or a signal to an AIO thread during a
    read: the process aborts on an `assert` → `RuntimeError: ... Bad file
    descriptor`, or the read completes.
    
    ---------
    
    Signed-off-by: Xinyu Lian <lian7@illinois.edu>
    Co-authored-by: Olatunji Ruwase <tunji.ruwase@snowflake.com>

commit 1b022dcd4d45782f0af5b106cb3a2b2ca1092e16
Author: Xinyu Lian <lian7@illinois.edu>
Date:   Sat Nov 7 08:48:22 2026 +0000

    DeepNVMe: fix silent I/O failures on misaligned buffers (#8985)
    
    ## Summary
    
    DeepNVMe does not check the result of an I/O request, so a request that
    the kernel fails is reported as done. ZeRO-Infinity reads and writes
    views into flat buffers at offsets that are often not 512-byte aligned,
    and O_DIRECT fails those on md RAID, LVM, and before Linux 6.0 on every
    block device. Swap-ins then leave stale data, swap-outs write nothing,
    and training goes on with wrong weights and gradients.
    
    This PR checks every completed request: a failed op makes `wait()`,
    `sync_pread()` and `sync_pwrite()` raise `RuntimeError` after the other
    ops complete. Tensors that are not contiguous, or not aligned as the
    file needs (`statx`, else 512), go through the existing bounce buffer.
    ZeRO-Infinity's fast init reads partitions of unaligned length through a
    padded staging tensor. Also, `io_submit` errors no longer abort on an
    assert, `io_pgetevents` is retried after `EINTR`, and a failed
    `io_queue_init` raises.
    
    ## Fixes
    
    Before → after, GH200, ext4 on md RAID 0, base `1a956270f`:
    
    1. I/O on a pinned view 416 bytes past an aligned address: nothing
    moved, success returned → data moved.
    2. ZeRO-3, NVMe parameter offload, Qwen2.5-0.5B: 60 of 290 parameters
    wrong after `initialize` → 0; the first loss now equals CPU offload's
    (12.206690).
    3. ZeRO-3, NVMe optimizer offload, 2 ranks, Qwen2.5 config: losses leave
    CPU offload's at step 2 → equal.
    4. A write past the file size limit: success with 2048 of 4096 bytes on
    disk → `RuntimeError: ... File too large`.
    5. A write to a read-only file, or a signal to an AIO thread during a
    read: the process aborts on an `assert` → `RuntimeError: ... Bad file
    descriptor`, or the read completes.
    
    ---------
    
    Signed-off-by: Xinyu Lian <lian7@illinois.edu>
    Co-authored-by: Olatunji Ruwase <tunji.ruwase@snowflake.com>

commit 1b022dcd4d45782f0af5b106cb3a2b2ca1092e16
Author: Xinyu Lian <lian7@illinois.edu>
Date:   Sat Nov 7 08:48:22 2026 +0000

    DeepNVMe: fix silent I/O failures on misaligned buffers (#8985)
    
    ## Summary
    
    DeepNVMe does not check the result of an I/O request, so a request that
    the kernel fails is reported as done. ZeRO-Infinity reads and writes
    views into flat buffers at offsets that are often not 512-byte aligned,
    and O_DIRECT fails those on md RAID, LVM, and before Linux 6.0 on every
    block device. Swap-ins then leave stale data, swap-outs write nothing,
    and training goes on with wrong weights and gradients.
    
    This PR checks every completed request: a failed op makes `wait()`,
    `sync_pread()` and `sync_pwrite()` raise `RuntimeError` after the other
    ops complete. Tensors that are not contiguous, or not aligned as the
    file needs (`statx`, else 512), go through the existing bounce buffer.
    ZeRO-Infinity's fast init reads partitions of unaligned length through a
    padded staging tensor. Also, `io_submit` errors no longer abort on an
    assert, `io_pgetevents` is retried after `EINTR`, and a failed
    `io_queue_init` raises.
    
    ## Fixes
    
    Before → after, GH200, ext4 on md RAID 0, base `1a956270f`:
    
    1. I/O on a pinned view 416 bytes past an aligned address: nothing
    moved, success returned → data moved.
    2. ZeRO-3, NVMe parameter offload, Qwen2.5-0.5B: 60 of 290 parameters
    wrong after `initialize` → 0; the first loss now equals CPU offload's
    (12.206690).
    3. ZeRO-3, NVMe optimizer offload, 2 ranks, Qwen2.5 config: losses leave
    CPU offload's at step 2 → equal.
    4. A write past the file size limit: success with 2048 of 4096 bytes on
    disk → `RuntimeError: ... File too large`.
    5. A write to a read-only file, or a signal to an AIO thread during a
    read: the process aborts on an `assert` → `RuntimeError: ... Bad file
    descriptor`, or the read completes.
    
    ---------
    
    Signed-off-by: Xinyu Lian <lian7@illinois.edu>
    Co-authored-by: Olatunji Ruwase <tunji.ruwase@snowflake.com>

commit 8af59b2e7a91c227081617240e98aa282eadc5f9
Author: Olatunji Ruwase <tunji.ruwase@snowflake.com>
Date:   Fri Nov 6 11:21:30 2026 +0000

    Restore fp32 masters for ZeRO-3 and the ZeRO-1 BF16 optimizer (#8892)
    
    ## Summary
    - Follow-up to #8891 (merged as `2dd22dc`). The delta against `master`
    is ZeRO-3 and the dedicated ZeRO-1 BF16 optimizer, plus the review fixes
    listed below.
    - `load_checkpoint` still always restores saved fp32 masters.
    `load_optimizer_states=False` keeps those masters and starts Adam with
    fresh moments. `load_module_only=True` rebuilds the dedicated BF16
    optimizer from the loaded bf16 weights. ZeRO-3 still reads its fp32
    partition on a module-only load, because the model checkpoint does not
    hold the partitioned weights.
    - `ZeRO-3` and `BF16_Optimizer.load_state_dict(...,
    load_from_fp32_weights=False)` now rebuild the masters from the bit16
    weights, matching ZeRO stage 1 and 2. `DeepSpeedEngine.load_checkpoint`
    passes true, so a normal resume keeps the saved masters.
    `zero_optimization.load_from_fp32_weights` stays deprecated and ignored.
    - Review fixes: a pipeline-serialized load now checks that ZeRO shards
    exist before waiting on the previous rank, so a missing shard raises
    instead of leaving ranks blocked in `dist.recv`. A universal load that
    skips optimizer state keeps `optim_fragment`, so
    `safe_get_full_optimizer_state` and `safe_set_full_optimizer_state`
    still work. A leftover debug `print` in `BF16_Optimizer` is removed.
    
    AI assistance was used to implement and test this change. This does not
    duplicate an open DeepSpeed PR.
    
    ## Test plan
    - [x] CPU, torch 2.9.1+cu130, Python 3.12.12, Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C,
    gloo, world size 1, `tests/unit/checkpoint/test_fp32_master_only.py` and
    `tests/unit/checkpoint/test_fp32_master_stage3_bf16.py`: 10 passed. Both
    files ran on the tree that became `a22f0cc4`.
    - The dedicated BF16 optimizer keeps the saved masters when optimizer
    state is skipped and rebuilds them for `load_module_only=True`. ZeRO-3
    keeps the saved masters for both of those loads. Adam moments stay
    fresh.
    - A direct `load_state_dict(..., load_from_fp32_weights=False)` after a
    module-only load rebuilds the masters from the bit16 weights, for both
    BF16 and ZeRO-3.
    - Optimizer globals (`clip_grad`, `overflow`, `dynamic_loss_scale`) are
    not restored on a masters-only load.
    - A universal masters-only load into a stepped engine keeps
    `safe_get_full_optimizer_state` and `safe_set_full_optimizer_state`
    working.
    - A pipeline-serialized load with missing shards raises before
    `dist.recv`. The NVMe masters-only copy restores only the fp32 swap
    file.
    - [x] 4×H200, torch 2.9.1+cu130, Python 3.12.12, same two files on tree
    `a22f0cc4`: 10 passed in 52s. This includes the three data-parallel
    change tests (universal, legacy, elastic), which spawn 2 ranks on
    `cuda:0`/`cuda:1`. The #8891 suite there does not cover these two
    optimizers.
    
    Validated cells: dedicated ZeRO-1 BF16 optimizer and ZeRO-3, same
    data-parallel size, legacy checkpoint, bf16, no offload. ZeRO-1/2
    universal masters-only load covered by the fragment test. Open cells:
    fp16, MoE, real NVMe offload (the NVMe test uses a stub swapper), and a
    data-parallel size change.
    
    ---------
    
    Signed-off-by: Olatunji Ruwase <tunji.ruwase@snowflake.com>
    Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

input.rationale: 增量更新（6d64e1b -> 02f7978，版本维持 0.19.10，共 10 个提交）：九单元主线结构不变，仍按「入门 -> 核心用法 -> 运行时基础设施 -> 混合精度 -> ZeRO 核心 -> 多维并行 -> 推理引擎 -> 高级机制 -> 内核工程」推进。本周期代码变化集中在五条线：一是 fp32 masters 的恢复语义补全（#8892）：ZeRO-3 的 _rigid_load_state_dict/_load_universal_checkpoint 新增 load_from_fp32_weights=False 分支并用 refresh_fp32_params() 从 bit16 权重重建分区，BF16_Optimizer 同场景调用 _restore_from_bit16_weights，引擎流水线串行加载先检查 ZeRO 分片存在再进入 dist.recv（缺失即 raise 而非死等），universal 加载跳过优化器状态时保留 optim_fragment 使 safe_get/set_full_optimizer_state 仍可用——u4-l3、u5-l8、u8-l3 相应 update。二是 AutoEP+AutoTP folding 的梯度裁剪修复（#8823）：折叠后 TP peers 各持不同路由专家，stage_1_and_2 的 get_grad_norm_direct 新增 process_group/expert_parallel_group 参数，_is_folded_expert_group（按 ds_zero_placement_family=="autoep_expert" 判定）的范数改为在实际 expert-DP 分区组与 EP owner 组上求和且不再做专家范数平均，稠密组与原生 MoE 组保持原路径并可与折叠组共存，契约写入 docs/code-docs/source/autoep.rst——u5-l3、u6-l6 update（u6-l6 同时并入 #9029 的 transformers _CanRecordRegistry dict 兼容）。三是两处卸载正确性修复：ZeRO-3 NVMe 参数预取去重（#9014，参数 trace 每次使用一条，末层 forward+backward、检查点重算与共享层双计导致 swap_in 二次分配缓冲断言）落在 partitioned_param_coordinator，u5-l5 update；DeepNVMe 静默 I/O 失败修复（#8985，完成请求结果检查抛 RuntimeError、非对齐/非连续走 bounce buffer、fast init 用填充 staging 读非对齐分区、EINTR 重试）重写 csrc/aio 与 optimizer_utils，u5-l7 update。四是 CPU 优化器状态精度（#8974）：DeepSpeedCPUAdam/Lion/Adagrad 改继承新基类 DeepSpeedCPUOptimizer，load_state_dict 用 restore_optimizer_state_dtype 把 fp32_optimizer_states 下的浮点状态恢复为 fp32，u5-l4 update。五是 Hybrid Engine 非贪婪采样进入快路径（#8939）：_token_selector 统一 graph decode/continuous batching/continuous batching+graph 三条路径的 token 选择（temperature<=0 argmax，否则按 generate() 顺序在 float32 logits 上应用 Temperature/TopK/TopP warper 后 multinomial），采样在 host 端图之外故图捕获不再要求 greedy，continuous batching 移除 temperature>0 拒绝且 repetition penalty 调整到 warper 之前，u7-l4 update。其余 CI/测试杂项（#9032 workflow exit code 5 处理、#9020 移除 deepspeed-kernels、#9028 测试改 forkserver）不改变任何讲义所教内容，全部 keep；u8-l7、u8-l8、u9-l5 上周期新增讲义尚未生成，维持 new。

units.title: 初识 DeepSpeed：定位、构建与启动

learning_goals: 写出 DeepSpeed 标准接入代码：初始化、引擎包装、train_batch 循环
解释 initialize() 如何依据模型/优化器/配置选择引擎类
复用 tests/unit/simple_model.py 的 SimpleModel 搭建本地实验台
minimal_modules: initialize 函数签名与引擎分发
参数args 与 config 双通道
lectures.practice_task: 仿照 tests/unit/simple_model.py，用 SimpleModel 写一个包含 engine.train_batch() 循环的最小训练脚本，配置 train_batch_size=8、micro_batch_size=4，跑通并打印每步 loss。
lectures.title: initialize() 与三步接入法
lectures.topic: 精读 deepspeed/__init__.py 中的 initialize()：参数如何解析、引擎类型如何选择（训练引擎/流水线引擎/推理引擎）、config 字符串与字典两种传入方式。

learning_goals: 掌握 train_batch_size、micro_batch_size、gradient_accumulation_steps 三者关系
追踪一个配置项从 JSON 到引擎属性的读取链路
了解 deterministic_mode 等新增顶层布尔开关在 _do_sanity_check 前经由 determinism.configure_determinism 挂载的方式
学会用 DeepSpeedConfigWriter 生成配置文件
lectures.practice_task: 手写一份包含 bf16、zero stage 2、offload 与 deterministic_mode 的完整 JSON 配置，加载进 DeepSpeedConfig 并断言 gradient_accumulation_steps 等推导值与手算一致，同时验证 deterministic_mode 属性被正确设置。
lectures.title: 配置系统：从 JSON 到 DeepSpeedConfig
lectures.topic: 解析 DeepSpeedConfig 如何校验并展开 JSON 配置的 batch size、优化器、调度器、并行度等字段，新增的 deterministic_mode 顶层开关如何在配置构造期被解析，以及 DeepSpeedConfigWriter 的反向生成能力。

learning_goals: 按顺序列出引擎构造的 8 个关键阶段
理解 optimizer、basic_optimizer、engine.optimizer 三层包装关系
说明 deterministic_mode 在引擎构造早期应用确定性策略的时机与前提（CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG 检查）
弄清 modules_to_save、external parameters、AutoTP 冻结参数记录（_autotp_frozen_replicated_params）等特殊注册机制在初始化中何时生效
lectures.practice_task: 在 DeepSpeedEngine.__init__ 中按执行顺序整理一份初始化阶段清单（配置、确定性策略、专家并行、AutoTP、ZeRO、优化器、检查点加载），并给每个阶段标注对应源码行号。
lectures.title: 引擎构造：DeepSpeedEngine.__init__ 全流程
lectures.topic: 逐段阅读 DeepSpeedEngine 构造函数：参数配置、确定性策略应用（deterministic_mode）、AutoEP/AutoTP 注入（含冻结参数记录）、优化器包装（fp16/bf16/ZeRO）、数据加载器、监控、检查点加载等阶段的先后顺序与交互。

learning_goals: 画出 train_batch 一次调用的内部时序图
解释 is_gradient_accumulation_boundary 对梯度同步频率的影响
描述 _backward_prologue 中对 AutoTP 冻结复制参数的防御性检查（unfreeze 后训练会静默漂移，引擎改为直接报错）
追踪 _take_model_step 的 fp32 梯度裁剪链路：clip_fp32_gradients -> clip_grad_norm_，以及 MoE 感知改造——专家参数不再对 DP 组求平均，而是在专家并行组上求范数（每个专家只计一次），并用一次世界组 all_reduce 投票保证所有 rank 走同一条集体通信路径
实现不带 DeepSpeed 引擎的手动 backward/step（unmanaged 模式）
minimal_modules: MoE 感知的梯度裁剪范数
lectures.practice_task: 在 simple_model 脚本中把默认循环改写为手动模式：调用 engine.backward(loss)、engine.step()，并对比与 engine.train_batch() 的 global_steps 推进差异；再配置 gradient_clipping 打印每步 total_norm，结合 clip_grad_norm_ 源码解释无 MoE 时范数为何要除以 DP world_size 再 all_reduce。
lectures.title: 训练主循环：train_batch、backward 与 step
lectures.topic: 追踪一次 train_batch 调用的完整链路：数据迭代、前向、loss 缩放、backward（含 _backward_prologue 中新增的 AutoTP 冻结参数检查）、梯度边界判定、梯度裁剪（fp32 路径经 clip_grad_norm_，MoE 参数在专家并行组上求范数）、优化器 step、LR 调度与监控写入。

units.title: 核心用法：initialize 与训练引擎

learning_goals: 列举 AbstractAccelerator 定义的 20+ 设备无关接口
解释 real_accelerator.py 的按环境变量/库探测加载机制
以 XPU 后端为例，说明一个 accelerator 如何绕过 torch、用 ctypes 直接驱动 Level Zero ext_memmap 扩展注册 pinned host memory
解释 is_graph_capture_supported 显式 opt-in 设计：默认 False（只暴露图 API 的后端留在 eager 路径），CUDA 返回 True 且要求先实现 is_current_stream_capturing（静态 KV cache 靠它跳过图捕获期间非法的 host 端检查）
理解 AGENTS 规则『禁止直接 import torch.distributed』背后的设计原因
minimal_modules: 图捕获能力的 opt-in 声明
XPU 的 Level Zero pinned memory 注册
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 abstract_accelerator.py 中的方法签名，挑 5 个关键方法（如 available_memory、communication_backend_name、is_graph_capture_supported）对比 cuda_accelerator.py 与 cpu_accelerator.py 的实现差异并列表总结；再对照 accelerator/xpu_accelerator.py 中新增的 _l0_loader 与 pinned memory 注册路径，总结「torch 通道不可用时后端自力更生」的实现模式。
lectures.title: 加速器抽象层：一套代码支持多种硬件
lectures.topic: 解读 AbstractAccelerator 接口与 real_accelerator 的运行时探测加载，DeepSpeed 如何用这层抽象同时支持 CUDA、CPU、HPU、XPU、NPU 等十余种后端；以 XPU 通过 Level Zero ZE_extension_external_memmap_sysmem 注册页锁定主机内存、以及图捕获能力改为按后端显式 opt-in（is_graph_capture_supported）为例展示后端深度适配。

learning_goals: 解释 comm 模块对 torch.distributed 的日志与监控包装
追踪 init_distributed 的 backend 协商与进程组建立过程

解读 TorchBackend 的两个 Gloo 兼容修复：_ensure_gloo_subgroup_split 兜底 PyTorch 2.7~2.10 对非成员 rank 调用 perform_nocolor_split（Gloo 未实现该 NCCL 专属方法）导致的 AttributeError；stage_on_cpu 把 CPU 暂存从仅 MPS 张量扩展到「进程组本身是 gloo 时的 CUDA 张量」（避免 writev EFAULT），并按签名解析出 group 判断后端
理解 dist = None 延迟绑定的设计意图
lectures.practice_task: 写脚本调用 deepspeed.comm.init_distributed 完成单机两进程初始化，打印 world_size 与 rank，并钩住 log_duration 观察一次 allreduce 的耗时输出；再用 backend=gloo 建组并对一个 CUDA 张量做 all_reduce，验证 stage_on_cpu 的 CPU 暂存路径被触发（可用日志或断点确认）。
lectures.title: deepspeed.comm：分布式通信统一入口
lectures.topic: 解析 comm 包如何包装 torch.distributed（nccl/gloo/mpi）并提供 init_distributed、allgather、reduce 等统一 API，ccl/mori 等非 CUDA 后端的适配方式，以及针对 Gloo 的子组拆分兜底与 CUDA 张量 CPU 暂存两个兼容层修复。

learning_goals: 推导给定 world_size 和各并行度时每个 rank 的分组结果
解释 expert data parallel 组与普通 data parallel 组的区别
掌握 _create_model_parallel/_create_expert_and_data_parallel 的调用时机
lectures.practice_task: 写一个纯函数模拟 groups 的 rank 分组算法：对 world_size=8、tp=2、ep=2 计算每个 rank 所属的 dp/tp/ep 组，并用小规模 torchrun 进程组实际验证。
lectures.title: 进程组管理：并行维度划分
lectures.topic: 精读 groups.py：data/tensor/pipeline/expert/zero 各并行维度的进程组如何创建、缓存与查询，这是 ZeRO 与所有并行策略的坐标系统。

learning_goals: 解析 hostfile 与 SSH 多节点命令拼装的完整流程
区分 multinode_runner 支持的 pdsh/标准 SSH/资源管理器模式
排查常见的多节点启动失败原因
lectures.practice_task: 编写一个单机模拟的 hostfile（两行 localhost 条目），用 deepspeed --hostfile 启动 2 节点 x 1 进程的简单任务，观察 runner 生成的实际命令行与环境变量。
lectures.title: 多节点启动：hostfile、SSH 与资源筛选
lectures.topic: 阅读 runner.py 的 hostfile 解析、include/exclude 资源筛选与 multinode_runner 的远端命令拼装，理解从 deepspeed 命令到每个节点 python 训练脚本的完整链路。

units.title: 运行时基础设施：加速器、通信与进程组

learning_goals: 解释动态 loss scaling 的溢出检测与 scaleFactor 调整规则
区分 initial_scale、min_loss_scale、scale_window 参数语义
追踪 scale/unscale 在引擎主循环中的调用点
lectures.practice_task: 在 CPU 上直接实例化 DynamicLossScaler，构造一个周期性溢出的假梯度序列，绘制 scale 值随 step 的变化曲线并验证调整规则。
lectures.title: fp16 与动态 loss scaling
lectures.topic: 解读 loss_scaler.py 中静态/动态 LossScaler：溢出检测、scale 窗口调整、scale_wrt_gas 的含义，以及 fp16 训练为何必须配合 loss scaling。

learning_goals: 描述 fp16 梯度到 fp32 主权重的拷贝时机
对比 fused 与 unfused 两条路径的适用条件
理解 zero_grad/step 在包装层中的委托关系
说明 initialize_optimizer_states 为何要在 param.device（而非当前加速器设备）上创建初始梯度：Adagrad 在构造期就初始化状态，设备错位会让 CPU/卸载参数直接报错
lectures.practice_task: 用一个两层 MLP 分别以 fused_adam=False/True 跑相同步数的 fp16 训练，打印每步 loss 与 loss scale，确认两条路径数值一致；再把 optimizer 换成 torch.optim.Adagrad 验证初始化路径（可参考 tests/unit/runtime/zero/test_zero_adagrad.py 的断言）。
lectures.title: FP16 包装优化器：unfused 与 fused 两条路径
lectures.topic: 对比 unfused_optimizer 与 fused_optimizer：如何维护 fp32 主权重、如何调用 FusedAdam 与 CPU 端变体、zero_grad/step 的包装逻辑，以及 initialize_optimizer_states 中 Adagrad 构造期初始化的设备修复。

learning_goals: 解释 bf16 无需 loss scaling 的数值原因
描述 bf16 主权重 + fp32 优化器状态的内存布局
说明 2025/12 引入的低精度 master states 的配置方式

解读本周期 load_state_dict 的 masters 恢复语义：load_from_fp32_weights=False 时调用 _restore_from_bit16_weights() 从 bit16 权重重建 fp32 主权重（与 ZeRO stage 1/2 对齐），而引擎 load_checkpoint 的正常恢复仍传 True 保留已保存的 masters，load_optimizer_states=False 则保留 masters 并让 Adam moments 重新开始
lectures.practice_task: 对同一个模型分别用 fp16 与 bf16 配置训练，对比每步显存占用（torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated）与最终 loss，解释差异来源；再参考 tests/unit/checkpoint/test_fp32_master_stage3_bf16.py，对 BF16_Optimizer 分别以 load_from_fp32_weights=True/False 调用 load_state_dict，断言前者保留保存的 fp32 masters、后者从 bit16 权重重建。
lectures.title: BF16 优化器与低精度主权重
lectures.topic: 解读 BF16_Optimizer：为何 bf16 不需要 loss scaling、fp32 主权重可选策略（keep_in_fp32）、低精度 master state 支持，以及本周期 load_state_dict 在 load_from_fp32_weights=False 时改为从 bit16 权重重建 masters 的恢复语义。

learning_goals: 跟踪引擎在 step 边界调用 scheduler.step 的位置
实现一个自定义 schedule 类型的注册/接入
排查 LR 不生效或重复推进的常见配置错误
lectures.practice_task: 实现一个带余弦退火加线性 warmup 的自定义 LR 函数，通过 params scheduler type LambdaLR 接入 DeepSpeed 训练，绘制实际 LR 曲线验证。
lectures.title: 学习率调度器体系
lectures.topic: 阅读 lr_schedules.py：WarmupLR/WarmupDecayLR 等内置调度器的实现，get_lr_scheduler 工厂，以及引擎如何在梯度累积边界推进调度器。

units.title: 混合精度与优化器包装体系

learning_goals: 用 memory=Ψ + KΨ + 2Ψ 公式解释三阶段的显存节省
列出 zero/config.py 中每个配置类对应的 JSON 字段
区分参数切分、梯度切分、优化器状态切分分别发生在哪些类
lectures.practice_task: 用 torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated 实测同一个模型在 ZeRO-0/1/2/3（单进程或 2 进程）下的峰值显存，写成对照表并附公式解释。
lectures.title: ZeRO 总览：三阶段与配置体系
lectures.topic: 综述 ZeRO 的动机（optimizer state/gradient/parameter 三级切分）与 DeepSpeed 中 zero 包的文件布局、配置类继承结构，为后续 7 篇建立框架。

learning_goals: 解释 partition_size=world_size 时参数 numel 的分桶逻辑
描述 alignment 与 max_num_params 对切分的影响
理解 NoGatherHandle 与常规 allgather 句柄的区别
lectures.practice_task: 用 zero.Init() 构建一个两层 Transformer，逐参数打印 ds_tensor 的形状与占空比，验证切分总量等于完整参数量，再尝试 gpu_id 与 remote_device 参数。
lectures.title: zero.Init：参数从出生就切分
lectures.topic: 精读 partition_parameters.py：模型构建期如何在线实例化即切分参数、padding/对齐策略、NoGather 优化以及 external parameter 注册。

learning_goals: 追踪 reduce 的流水线深度与 bucket 生成算法
解释 deepspeed.zero 梯度平均化的两种模式
定位 step 中 flatten/reduce_scatter/allgather 的调用顺序
说明 Adagrad 初始化修复：为何改用 self.optimizer.param_groups（而非 single_partition_of_fp32_groups）重建优化器，以保留每个参数自己的选项
理解低精度 master（low_precision_master_weights_and_grads）从 CPU 恢复梯度前先 dest_buffer.zero_() 的原因：共享 scratch 里残留的上一步 NaN 会被溢出检查读到

解读本周期折叠专家（AutoEP+AutoTP folding）的梯度裁剪修复：get_grad_norm_direct 新增 process_group/expert_parallel_group 参数，_is_folded_expert_group（组内参数 ds_zero_placement_family 全为 autoep_expert）的范数改为在实际 expert-DP 分区组与 EP owner 组上求和，且 _average_expert_grad_norms 不再对折叠组做专家范数平均——折叠后 TP peers 各持不同路由专家，旧的「过滤到 TP rank 0」路径会漏掉专家属主；稠密组与原生 MoE 组（含两者共存）保持原路径
minimal_modules: 低精度恢复的 scratch 清零
折叠专家的梯度范数组
lectures.practice_task: 在两卡 ZeRO-2 训练中把 IPG bucket 调成不同大小（通过 contiguous_gradients 与 overlap_comm 组合），对比每步耗时与通信量，解释 bucket 对吞吐的影响；再开启低精度 master states + offload，构造一次人为溢出后恢复，验证 scratch 清零后不再误报 overflow；最后阅读 tests/unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_autotp_sharded_attention.py 中 TestShardedAttentionClippedUpdate 的对照断言（折叠切分下的实际 SGD 更新 vs 未切分 ZeRO-0 参考），解释折叠专家组为何不能走专家范数平均。
lectures.title: ZeRO-1/2：梯度切分与 IPG 流水线
lectures.topic: 精读 stage_1_and_2.py 的 DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer：独立并行梯度（IPG）bucket、overlap 通信、梯度 reduce-scatter 与扁平化缓冲区管理，Adagrad 用 param_groups 重建、低精度梯度恢复前清空共享 scratch，以及本周期折叠专家的梯度范数改为在 expert-DP 分区组与 EP owner 组上求和的裁剪修复。

learning_goals: 描述 offload 时优化器状态、梯度和参数分别驻留在哪类内存
解释 pinned memory 在 CPU 优化器中的作用
对比 fused CPU 优化器与 torch CPU 优化器的性能差异

说明本周期 DeepSpeedCPUAdam/CPULion/CPUAdagrad 改为继承新基类 DeepSpeedCPUOptimizer（deepspeed/ops/cpu_optimizer.py）：fp32_optimizer_states 开启时（默认）step 以 fp32 维护状态，但 torch 的 load_state_dict 会把状态 cast 成参数 dtype，基类覆盖它并用 utils/torch.restore_optimizer_state_dtype 把浮点状态恢复为 fp32，bf16/fp16 卸载恢复不再被静默降成低精度 moments
lectures.practice_task: 写一个直接使用 DeepSpeedCPUAdam 的基准脚本：在 CPU 上对 1M 参数向量分别用 torch.optim.Adam 与 DeepSpeedCPUAdam 各跑 100 步并对比耗时；再用 bf16 参数 + fp32_optimizer_states=True 构造 DeepSpeedCPUAdam，保存/加载 state_dict 后断言 exp_avg/exp_avg_sq 仍为 torch.float（参考 tests/unit/ops/adam/test_cpu_adam.py 的断言）。
lectures.title: ZeRO-Offload：CPU 卸载与 cpu_adam
lectures.topic: 解读 ZeRO-Offload 的实现：优化器状态与 fp32 梯度卸载到 CPU pinned memory、cpu_adam 内核的调用方式、单一/双重 offload 的区别，以及本周期新增 DeepSpeedCPUOptimizer 公共基类让 load_state_dict 保留 fp32 优化器状态的精度修复。

learning_goals: 解释参数 module hook（pre/post forward）触发 allgather 的机制
描述参数 ds_status 生命周期（AVAILABLE/INFLIGHT/NOT_AVAILABLE）
理解 hidden size 对齐与 contiguous 分配如何减少碎片
解读 zero/linear.py 中 LinearFunctionForZeroStage3 的 autocast 设备修复：设备类型跟随操作数所在设备而非当前加速器（CPU autocast 在 CUDA 机器上也必须正确生效），前向的设备选择被缓存到 ctx 供反向复用

解读本周期 NVMe 预取去重修复（#4072）：参数 trace 按「每次使用」记录一条，末层（forward 后紧跟 backward）、梯度检查点重算层与共享层都会在预取窗口内出现两次，__prefetch_nvme_param_partitions 现在用集合跳过重复参数，避免 swap_in() 第二次分配缓冲触发 param already assigned swap buffer 断言
minimal_modules: ZeRO-3 Linear 的 autocast 设备判定
lectures.practice_task: 在 ZeRO-3 训练中给一个自定义 Module 加 forward_pre_hook，打印触发时参数的 ds_status 与 ds_tensor 形状，验证参数按需物化过程；再参考 tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero_functorch_linear.py，在 CPU 张量 + torch.autocast('cpu') 场景下验证 LinearFunctionForZeroStage3 前后向 dtype 一致；最后阅读 tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero3_nvme_param_prefetch.py 的双计参数回归，说明去重修复前后的行为差异。
lectures.title: ZeRO-3：参数卸载与参数协调器
lectures.topic: 解读 parameter_offload.py 与 partitioned_param_coordinator.py：module hook 如何按需 allgather 参数、预取下一层参数、parameter_offload 的 ds_status 状态机、NVMe 预取窗口的重复参数去重修复，以及 zero/linear.py 中 ZeRO-3 定制 Linear 的 autocast 设备类型修复。

learning_goals: 列出 stage3 step 中 reduce_scatter 参数梯度与更新 ds_tensor 的顺序
解释 contiguous_memory_allocator 如何降低碎片
说明 partial offload 时子组设备串如何通过公共 accelerator API（device_name()）而非私有 _name 构造

解读 aliased_fp32_sub_groups：当权重已是 master dtype（fp32 模型，含 autocast 场景）时 fp32 分区直接复用权重分区，offload_states/reload_states 中这些子组没有独立存储、必须随 lp_params 一起搬运（_point_aliased_fp32_partitions_at_lp_buffer），单独 offload hp_params 不省显存并触发 warning_once
理解 reduce_scatter 配置项对性能的影响
lectures.practice_task: 用 partitioned_param_profiler（或手动计时）统计一次 stage3 step 中梯度 reduce 与参数更新各占的时间，调整 reduce_bucket_size 观察变化；再参考 tests/unit/v1/zero/test_offload_states.py，对一个 fp32 模型分别调用 offload_states(include=[hp_params]) 与 offload_states(include=[lp_params])，对照日志验证 aliased 子组只随 lp_params 移动。
lectures.title: ZeRO-3 优化器：stage3 主循环与连续内存
lectures.topic: 精读 stage3.py 的 DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer_Stage3：step 中梯度 reduce-scatter、参数按分区更新、partial offload 子组设备分配（用 get_accelerator().device_name() 公共接口）、contiguous memory 分配、「权重分区即 master 副本」（aliased_fp32_sub_groups）对 offload_states/reload_states 的改造与与 stage1/2 共享的 loss scaling 机制。

learning_goals: 描述 PartitionedParamSwapper 的读写队列与线程模型
解释 aio 样本缓冲、线程数、块大小等调优参数的含义
理解参数从 NVMe->CPU->GPU 的两级流水

解读本周期 DeepNVMe 静默 I/O 失败修复：wait()/sync_pread()/sync_pwrite() 现在检查每个完成请求的结果并抛 RuntimeError（写满文件、只读文件等不再假装成功）；非连续或未按文件所需对齐（statx 探测、缺省 512 字节）的张量改走 bounce buffer；优化器 fast init 对非对齐长度分区用填充 staging 张量读整块再 narrow 拷出；io_submit 错误不再 assert、io_pgetevents 处理 EINTR 重试、io_queue_init 失败抛错
minimal_modules: I/O 结果检查与错误传播
lectures.practice_task: 运行 deepspeed 的 nvme 性能探测（参考 deepspeed/nvme/parse_nvme_stats.py 对输出格式的定义）对自己的磁盘做一次测速，确定最优线程数/块大小组合；再阅读 tests/unit/v1/nvme/test_aio.py 中未对齐视图与错误注入（写满文件、只读文件）用例，对照修复前后行为说明为什么 O_DIRECT 下错位缓冲会静默丢数据。
lectures.title: ZeRO-Infinity：NVMe 交换与异步 IO
lectures.topic: 解读 swap_tensor 包与 nvme/io_engine：参数/优化器状态在 GPU/CPU/NVMe 三级存储间的交换、异步 IO 内核（csrc/aio）与 pipelined swapper 的实现，以及本周期 DeepNVMe 对齐/错误检查修复（完成请求结果校验、bounce buffer、staging 读取、EINTR 重试）。

learning_goals: 解释为何训练时只有 rank0 持有完整优化器状态也能恢复
用 zero_to_fp32.py 从 ZeRO 检查点提取可部署的单文件模型
理解 tensor_fragment 如何只读必要分片加速导出

解读本周期 fp32 masters 的恢复矩阵：引擎 load_checkpoint 的正常恢复总是加载保存的 fp32 masters；load_optimizer_states=False 保留 masters 并让 Adam moments 重新开始；load_module_only=True 时 ZeRO-3 仍读取 fp32 分区（模型检查点不含分区权重）；stage3 的 _rigid_load_state_dict/_load_universal_checkpoint 新增 load_from_fp32_weights=False 分支，用 refresh_fp32_params() 从 bit16 权重重建分区
说明流水线串行加载的分片预检查：进入 dist.recv 等待前先确认 ZeRO 分片存在，缺失时直接 raise 而非让各 rank 死等
minimal_modules: 流水线加载的分片预检查
lectures.practice_task: 跑一次两卡 ZeRO-2 训练，保存检查点后用 python -m deepspeed.utils.zero_to_fp32（或等价 API）导出完整 fp32 权重，加载回单进程模型验证权重一致性；再参考 tests/unit/checkpoint/test_fp32_master_only.py，分别以 load_optimizer_states=False 与 load_module_only=True 加载，断言 masters 的保留/重建行为符合恢复矩阵。
lectures.title: ZeRO 检查点保存与权重导出
lectures.topic: 解读引擎 save/load_checkpoint 对 ZeRO 分片状态的处理：优化器状态/参数/调度器状态如何按 rank 保存、zero_to_fp32 如何按需重组出完整 fp32 权重，以及本周期 fp32 masters 恢复矩阵的补全（masters-only/module-only 加载语义、stage3 从 bit16 权重重建、流水线串行加载的分片预检查）。

units.title: ZeRO 显存优化（核心单元）

learning_goals: 解释 AutoTPMeta 如何从模型 config 推断切分维度，以及 training 字段如何让每个模型记住自己被切分时的训练模式
解释 training_mode=None 时层按模型级而非进程级跟随 set_autotp_mode 的语义（冻结 teacher + 训练 student 共存于一个进程）
理解 register_replicated_grad_hooks 对冻结参数（requires_grad=False）跳过注册并返回清单、引擎在 backward 前拒绝后续 unfreeze 的防御逻辑
对比推理注入与训练模式下 TP 的不同实现路径
实现一个自定义 policy 适配自己的模型结构
minimal_modules: AutoTPMeta 切分与 training 模式推断
冻结参数的梯度 all-reduce 处理
lectures.practice_task: 用 HuggingFace 的小模型（如 sshleifer/tiny-gpt2）开 tensor_parallel.size=2，遍历替换后的模型打印每个线性层的 in/out features，验证按 head 切分是否正确；再做一个实验：把某层参数 freeze 后传入 AutoTP（training_mode 显式指定），观察 register_replicated_grad_hooks 的跳过清单与引擎 backward 时的报错信息。
lectures.title: AutoTP：自动张量并行注入
lectures.topic: 解读 module_inject 包：如何按 policy 识别模型中的线性/注意力层，tp_shard 如何按 head 维度切分权重并注入并行版 Linear；按模型管理 AutoTP 训练模式（AutoTPMeta.training、TensorParallel_Layer.is_training_mode 的 per-model 语义）与冻结模型支持（frozen replicated params 的跳过与引擎侧 unfreeze 防线）。

learning_goals: 推导 Ulysses 对 attention 输入输出形状的变换
解释为什么 Ulysses 能把通信量降到与 head 数相关
